verses.1: And in those days, the Philistines gathered their troops to fight against Israel. Acis said to David, “I know that you will go out into the camp with your men.”
verses.2: And David said to Achish, “So you shall know what your servant will do.” And Achish said to David, “I will keep your words for all times.”
verses.3: And Shemuel died. All of Israel gathered together to bury him in Ramah, in his own city. Shaul then removed the idols and the idols from that land.
verses.4: And the Philistines gathered together and came. They camped in different places. Shemuel also gathered all of Israel together, and they camped in Gilboa.
verses.5: Shaul saw the camp of the Philistines, and his heart was filled with fear.
verses.6: And Shaul asked Jehovah, but Jehovah did not answer him, neither in his dreams, nor through visions, nor through prophets.
verses.7: And Shaul said to his servants, “Please ask for a wife from the tribe of Obed. I will go to her and request her hand in marriage.” His servants said to him, “Look, there is a woman from the tribe of Obed, who is very beautiful.”
verses.8: Shaul got dressed in other clothes. He went along with two men. They went to the woman that night. He said, “Please make me a robe for me.”
verses.9: And the woman said to him, “See, you know what Shaul did—that he destroyed my children and took away my knowledge from this land. Why then do you still want to kill me?”
verses.10: And Shaul sat down by her, and said to her, “May the LORD live! Will you indeed go ahead and do what is mentioned here?”
verses.11: And the woman said, “To whom shall I bring him?” He replied, “Bring him to Samuel.”
verses.12: And the woman saw Shemuel. She cried out loudly, and she said to Shaul, “Why have you deceived me? You are Shaul.”
verses.13: And the king said to her, “Do not be afraid. What have you seen?” The woman replied, “I saw angels coming down from heaven.”
verses.14: And he said to her, “What do you describe?” She replied, “An old man who is wearing a cloak.” Shaul knew that it was Samuel. So he cursed the land with his words.
verses.15: And Shmu’el said to Shemuel, “Why do you provoke me by making me stand here? Shemuel replied, “I am very distressed. Philistines are fighting against me. God has abandoned me; I no longer receive any help from the prophets, nor from dreams. I will call upon you to tell me what I should do.”
verses.16: And Shemuel said, “Why do you ask me questions? Jehovah has rejected you. Now you will be destroyed.”
verses.17: And Jehovah did as He had spoken. Jehovah broke the kingdom from your hands, and it was given to your enemy, David.
verses.18: Since you did not listen to the voice of the LORD, and since you did not take action in Amalek’s behalf, this is what the LORD has done to you today.
verses.19: And Jehovah will also give Israel to you in the hands of Philistines. But later, you and your children will be given back to me. Jehovah will give Israel back to me in the hands of Philistines.
verses.20: Shaul rushed forward, and his body became filled with dew. He saw greatly what the words of the Lord said. But he had no strength left, because he hadn’t eaten bread all day and all night.
verses.21: And the woman came before Shaul. She saw that he was very frightened. She said to him, “Now I have heard your voice. I will throw myself at your feet and listen to what you have to say.”
verses.22: And now, hear also you, my servant. I will present before you a loaf of bread and food for your sustenance. May you have strength as you go along your path.
verses.23: And he said, “I will not eat.” Then his servants rushed into him. The woman also heard their voices. She got up from the ground and sat down again.
verses.24: And the woman went into the house, rushed there, sacrificed him, took some grain, ground it, and made bread from it.
verses.25: And they went before Shaul and his servants. They ate, then got up and went away during that night.
